items.title: Eddie Metz Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, October 3, 2015

ctx.x: Yeah. And there’s one point where he sounds like he’s the horn section of the Basie band. He’s playing [scats].

He’s amazing. He’s totally amazing. He has the technical prowess to play anything that comes to his mind. But he’s heavily influenced by the older guys: Willie “The Lion,” Basie, Jelly Roll Morton, as players. Fats Waller as a player. You know Basie, everybody thinks of him as just kind of going plink-plink-plink-plink. He was the most feared guy on 52nd Street in his day. He could really play. Listen to “The Kid From Red Bank.” It’s unbelievable. He’s playing stride. He studied with Fats Waller. So he knew how…
